items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the public authorities law, in relation to requiring at least
one electric charging station for every one hundred fifty thousand New York
state residents
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S749

SPONSOR: SEPULVEDA
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public authorities law, in relation to requiring at
least one electric charging station for every one hundred fifty thousand
New York state residents

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To establish a minimum number of publicly available electric vehicle
charging stations per residents.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends subdivision 9-a of section 1005 of the public authori-
ties law to mandate that the New York Power Authority be responsible for
the installation and operation of electric vehicle charging stations per
every 150,000 residents in the state.

Section 2 provides the effective date

 
DIFFERENCE BETWEEN ORIGINAL AND AMENDED VERSION (IF APPLICABLE):

This amendment adds a prevailing wage requirement.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Consumer surveys have shown that one of the biggest barriers to the
adoption of electric vehicles is inadequate charging infrastructure.
With overreliance on fossil fuels worsening our climate crisis, electric
vehicles must increasingly play a role in our daily lives.  The New York
Power Authority has an existing statutory goal to install publicly
available electric vehicle chargers. This legislation attaches a minimum
number of stations for residents to ensure that the resulting infras-
tructure truly increases the viability of electric vehicle ownership in
New York.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

S.2220 of 2021-22: Referred to Energy and Telecommunications

S.8100-A of 2020: Referred to Energy and Telecommunications

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately after becoming law.

summary: Requires at least one electric level three fast charging station available to the public for every five thousand New York state residents on a county level by December 31, 2026; provides for the siting of such charging stations; requires construction and development of such stations to comply with article 8 of the labor law including payment of the prevailing wage.
